batchName: Empire: Augustus and the Principate (27 BC-AD 14) - Latin words
chapterName: Empire: Augustus and the Principate (27 BC-AD 14)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: What does the name Augustus mean?
questions.explanation: It carried a religious glow, hinting that he stood close to the gods.

questions.question: What did the Romans call the disaster in the Teutoburg Forest?
options: The Clades Variana, the Varian Disaster
questions.explanation: Three legions were lost, and Rome gave up conquest beyond the Rhine.
questions.sourceQuote: The Romans called it the Varian Disaster (*Clades Variana*).

questions.question: By AD 13 Augustus’s troops had hailed him imperator 21 times. What did it mean?
questions.sourceQuote: his troops had hailed him as victorious general (*imperator*) 21 times.

questions.question: What did tribunicia potestas, granted to Augustus for life, let him do?
options: Summon the Senate and assemblies, propose laws and veto decisions
questions.explanation: It was the authority of the ancient tribunes who protected ordinary citizens.
questions.sourceQuote: Tribunician power (*tribunicia potestas*), the authority of the ancient tribunes who protected ordinary citizens, was granted for life.

questions.question: What was the aerarium militare that Augustus set up in AD 6?
options: A military treasury to pay soldiers and fund their retirement
questions.explanation: He donated 170 million sesterces to start it.
questions.sourceQuote: In AD 6 he set up a military treasury (*aerarium militare*)

questions.question: In 12 BC Augustus became pontifex maximus. What was that?
options: Chief priest, head of Rome’s state religion
questions.explanation: In 2 BC the Senate also named him Father of the Fatherland.
questions.sourceQuote: In 12 BC he became chief priest (*pontifex maximus*), head of Rome's state religion.

questions.question: What did imperium proconsulare maius give Augustus?
options: Power over every governor in the empire
The right to be consul every year
A seat for life in the Senate
questions.explanation: It was part of the second settlement of 23 BC, when he gave up the consulship.
questions.sourceQuote: Greater proconsular power (*imperium proconsulare maius*) made him the superior of every governor in the empire.

questions.question: What were Augustus’s reported last words, Acta est fabula, plaudite?
options: “I found Rome brick and left it marble”
questions.explanation: He died at Nola, near Naples, on 19 August AD 14, aged 75.
questions.sourceQuote: "The play is over; applaud" (*Acta est fabula, plaudite*).
